html:
The Hurrians were a people of northern Mesopotamia and eastern Anatolia, in the hills and plains along the upper Tigris and Khabur rivers. On the map for 3000 and 2000 BCE their kingdoms lie north of the Mesopotamian city-states.

Their language belongs to no known family except Urartian, spoken later by Urartu. They are known from the 2000s BCE, when a Hurrian kingdom ruled from Urkesh, a city at today's Tell Mozan in Syria. Kings of the Akkadian Empire married into its royal family.

Later, from about 1550 BCE, a Hurrian kingdom called Mitanni became one of the great powers, trading letters and princesses with Egypt, until the Hittites and Assyria broke it in the 1300s. Hurrian gods and myths passed into Hittite religion, among them the story of the god Kumarbi.
